items.stem: Using 100 units of insolation, show with calculations how the heat budget of the earth balances.
items.answer: 35 units reflected (albedo); 14 absorbed by atmosphere; 51 by surface (100 − 35 − 14). The surface radiates 51: 17 to space, 34 to atmosphere. The atmosphere radiates 14 + 34 = 48 to space. Total outgoing = 17 + 48 = 65 = units absorbed, so the budget balances.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for 35/14/51, 1 for 17 + 34, 1 for 48 and the balance 65 = 65.

items.stem: The temperature at sea level at a place is 27°C. Assuming the normal lapse rate of 6.5°C per 1,000 m, what will be the temperature at a height of 5,000 m?

A hill station at 2,500 m records a temperature of 5°C. Using the normal lapse rate, calculate the expected temperature at a town in the plains at 200 m at the same time, and state one reason why actual temperatures may differ.
items.answer: Difference in height = 2,300 m; temperature difference = 6.5 × 2,300 ÷ 1,000 = 14.95°C. Temperature in the plains ≈ 5 + 14.95 = 19.95°C. Actual values may differ because of inversion of temperature, aspect, winds or cloud cover.
